exposure: COVID-19 pandemic period (2020) vs. prepandemic period (2017-2019)
Specific pandemic phases (first lockdown, second lockdown, period of less-vigorous restrictions)
outcome: causes of preterm births (e.g., history of serious disease, pathologic cardiotocography, intrauterine infection, history of preterm birth, multiple pregnancies, serious or severe psychological distress, preeclampsia, eclampsia, or hemolysis, elevated liver enzymes, and low platelet count syndrome)
cohort: The study included all births (184,827 total) registered in Hesse, Germany, from 2017 to 2020.
finding: The odds of very preterm births were lower during the COVID-19 pandemic period compared to the prepandemic period, with the greatest reduction observed during the second lockdown period.
